units.literal: The level platform, pearl-drop boards, wheel spokes, and wheel rims were all the same as the jade carriage.

units.zh: 輅亭高六尺四寸有奇， 紅髹四柱，長五尺四寸。
units.en: The carriage pavilion stood a little over six feet four inches high, with four red-lacquered pillars five feet four inches long.
units.literal: The carriage pavilion was a little over six feet four inches high, with four pillars lacquered red, five feet four inches long.

units.zh: 檻座上四周線金五彩香草板。
units.en: The railing base bore gold-thread five-colored herb panels on all four sides.
units.literal: On the railing seat on all four sides were gold-thread five-colored herb panels.

units.zh: 前左右有門，高五尺有奇， 廣二尺四寸有奇。
units.en: Doors to the front left and right stood a little over five feet high and a little over two feet four inches wide.
units.literal: To the front left and right were doors a little over five feet high and a little over two feet four inches wide.

units.zh: 門旁槅各二，編紅線條及明栨，皆紅髹。
units.en: Beside each door stood two panels woven with red cord and open lattices, all lacquered red.
units.literal: Beside each door were two panels, woven with red cord strips and open lattices, all lacquered red.

units.zh: 後五山屏鳳，青地 上雕木貼金龍五，間以五彩雲文。
units.en: At the rear stood a five-peak screen with five carved gilt dragons on blue ground, alternating with five-colored cloud motifs.
units.literal: At the rear was a five-peak screen; on blue ground were five carved wood applique gilt dragons, alternating with five-colored cloud patterns.

units.zh: 屏後紅髹板，皆抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。
units.en: Behind the screen, red-lacquered panels were all fitted with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.
units.literal: Behind the screen were red-lacquered panels, all set with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.

units.zh: 紅髹匡 軟座，紅絨墜座，大索四，下垂蓮花墜石，上施紅毯紅錦褥席。
units.en: It had a red-lacquered soft seat with red plush pendants, four great ropes with lotus pendant stones hanging below, and red carpet and brocade mats above.
units.literal: A red-lacquered frame soft seat, red plush pendant seat, four great ropes, lotus-flower pendant stones hanging below; above were spread red carpet and red brocade mat and cushion.

units.zh: 紅髹椅一，納板 一併褥。
units.en: There was one red-lacquered chair with a receiving panel and cushions.
units.literal: One red-lacquered chair, one receiving panel together with cushions.

units.zh: 椅中紅織金綺靠坐褥，四周有椅裙，施紅羅帷幔，外用青綺緣邊。
units.en: The chair held red gold-woven damask back and seat cushions with a skirt on all four sides, red gauze curtains within, and green damask edging outside.
units.literal: Within the chair were red gold-woven damask back and seat cushions; on all four sides was a chair skirt; red gauze curtains were hung; outside green damask bordered the edges.

units.zh: 紅簾 十二扇。
units.en: Twelve red curtain panels hung in place.
units.literal: Twelve panels of red curtains.

units.zh: 椅雕貼金龍彩雲，下線金彩雲板一。
units.en: The chair bore a carved gilt dragon among colored clouds, with one gold-thread cloud panel below.
units.literal: On the chair was carved an applique gilt dragon with colored clouds; below was one gold-thread colored-cloud panel.

units.zh: 亭內編紅線條。
units.en: Red cord strips were woven within the pavilion.
units.literal: Within the pavilion were woven red cord strips.

units.zh: 輅頂並圓盤，高二 尺五寸有奇，又鍍金銅寶珠頂，帶仰覆蓮座，高九寸，垂攀頂紅線圓條四。
units.en: The carriage top and round disk together rose a little over two feet five inches, capped by a gilt-bronze jeweled finial with upturned and downturned lotus seats nine inches high and four red cord roundels hanging from the finial.
units.literal: The carriage top and round disk together were a little over two feet five inches high; further, a gilt-bronze precious-pearl finial, with upturned and downturned lotus seat, nine inches high, and four red cord round strips hanging from the climbing top.

units.zh: 盤上 丹漆，下內外皆青地繪雲文，以青飾輅蓋。
units.en: The disk was cinnabar-lacquered above; inside and below, blue-ground cloud paintings trimmed the carriage canopy in blue.
units.literal: Above the disk was cinnabar lacquer; below, inside and outside, were all cloud patterns painted on blue ground, with blue used to ornament the carriage canopy.

units.zh: 亭內周圍青斗拱，承以丹漆匡，寶蓋 鬥以八頂，冒以紅綺，頂心繡雲龍，餘繡五彩雲文。
units.en: Green bracket sets lined the pavilion interior, borne on a cinnabar-lacquered frame; the precious canopy joined in eight peaks and covered in red damask, with cloud dragons at the apex and five-colored clouds elsewhere.
units.literal: Within the pavilion on all sides were green bracket sets, borne on a cinnabar-lacquered frame; the precious canopy was joined in eight peaks, covered with red damask; at the apex center cloud-dragons were embroidered, the rest embroidered with five-colored cloud patterns.

units.zh: 天輪三層皆紅髹，上雕木貼 金邊耀葉板七十二片，內飾青地雕木貼金雲龍文三層，間繪五彩雲襯板七十二片， 四周黃銅裝釘。
units.en: The three red-lacquered heaven-wheel layers bore seventy-two carved gilt-edged radiant leaf plates above, three layers of carved gilt cloud dragons on blue within, seventy-two painted cloud backing plates between, and yellow-bronze nail fittings on all four sides.
units.literal: The heaven-wheel's three layers were all lacquered red; above were seventy-two carved wooden gilt-edged radiant leaf plates; within were three layers of carved wooden applique gilt cloud-dragon patterns on blue ground, alternating with seventy-two painted five-colored cloud backing plates; on all four sides were yellow-bronze nail fittings.

units.zh: 上施紅綺瀝水三層，每層七十二摺，間繡五彩雲龍文。
units.en: Three layers of red damask drip panels hung above, each with seventy-two folds and embroidered five-colored cloud dragons between.
units.literal: Above were set three layers of red damask drip-water hangings, each layer of seventy-two folds, embroidered between with five-colored cloud-dragon patterns.

units.zh: 四角之飾 與大輅同，第圓條用紅線。
units.en: The corner ornaments matched the Great Carriage, though the round strips were red cord.
units.literal: The corner ornaments were the same as on the Great Carriage, but the round strips used red cord.

units.zh: 輅亭前一字闌干一扇，後一字帶轉角闌干一扇，左右 闌干二扇，內嵌五彩雲板，皆丹漆。
units.en: Before the carriage pavilion stood one single-bar balustrade panel and one single-bar corner panel behind; two balustrade panels left and right, all cinnabar-lacquered with inset five-colored cloud panels.
units.literal: Before the carriage pavilion one single-bar balustrade panel; behind one single-bar corner-turning balustrade panel; left and right two balustrade panels each; within were inset five-colored cloud panels, all cinnabar lacquer.

units.zh: 計十四柱，柱首制與大輅同。
units.en: There were fourteen pillars in all, their capitals matching the Great Carriage.
units.literal: In all fourteen pillars; the pillar-head form was the same as on the Great Carriage.

units.zh: 亭後建紅旗二， 以紅羅爲之。
units.en: Two red gauze flags were erected behind the pavilion.
units.literal: Behind the pavilion were erected two red flags, made of red gauze.

units.zh: 九斿，每斿內外繡升龍一。
units.en: Each of the nine streamers was embroidered inside and out with an ascending dragon.
units.literal: Nine streamers; on each streamer inside and outside was embroidered one ascending dragon.

units.zh: 左旗腰繡日月北斗，竿用抹金銅龍首。
units.en: The left flag's midsection bore embroidered sun, moon, and Northern Dipper motifs on a pole capped with a gilt-bronze dragon head.
units.literal: On the left flag's waist were embroidered sun, moon, and the Northern Dipper; the pole used a gilt-bronze dragon head.

units.zh: 右旗腰繡黻字，竿用抹金銅戟。
units.en: The right flag's midsection bore the fu character on a pole topped with a gilt-bronze halberd.
units.literal: On the right flag's waist was embroidered the fu character; the pole used a gilt-bronze halberd.

units.zh: 綴抹金銅鈴二，垂紅纓。
units.en: Two gilt-bronze bells were attached, with red tassels hanging below.
units.literal: Two gilt-bronze bells were attached; red tassels hung down.

units.zh: 其踏梯、行馬之屬，與 玉輅同。
units.en: Its mounting ladder, traveling-horse frames, and the like matched the jade carriage.
units.literal: Its mounting ladder, traveling-horse frames, and the like were the same as the jade carriage.

units.zh: 帳房用青木棉布，竿首青綠蹲猊，餘同乘輿帳房。
units.en: The tent chamber used blue cotton on wooden frames, with a blue-green crouching lion at the pole top; otherwise it matched the imperial carriage tent chamber.
units.literal: The tent chamber used blue cotton cloth on wooden frames; at the pole top a blue-green crouching lion; the rest was the same as the imperial carriage tent chamber.

units.zh: 東宮妃車，亦曰鳳轎、小轎，制同皇妃。
units.en: The Eastern Palace consort's carriage, also called the phoenix or small palanquin, followed the imperial consort's specifications.
units.literal: The Eastern Palace consort's carriage, also called the phoenix palanquin or small palanquin, was made the same as the imperial consort's.

units.zh: 行障、坐障之制亦同。
units.en: Its traveling and seated screens followed the same specifications.
units.literal: The specifications for traveling screens and seated screens were also the same.

units.zh: 親王象輅，其高視金輅減六寸，其廣減一尺。
units.en: The imperial prince's ivory carriage stood six inches lower and one foot narrower than the crown prince's gold carriage.
units.literal: The imperial prince's ivory carriage: its height compared with the gold carriage was reduced by six inches; its width reduced by one foot.

units.zh: 轅長視大輅減一尺。
units.en: Its shafts were one foot shorter than those of the Great Carriage.
units.literal: The shaft length compared with the Great Carriage was reduced by one foot.

units.zh: 輅座高三 尺有奇，餘飾同金輅。
units.en: The carriage body rose a little over three feet; otherwise its ornament matched the gold carriage.
units.literal: The carriage seat was a little over three feet high; the remaining ornament was the same as the gold carriage.

units.zh: 輅亭高五尺二寸有奇，紅髹四柱。
units.en: The carriage pavilion stood a little over five feet two inches high, with four red-lacquered pillars.
units.literal: The carriage pavilion was a little over five feet two inches high, with four pillars lacquered red.

units.zh: 檻座上四周紅髹條環板。
units.en: The railing base bore red-lacquered strip ring panels on all four sides.
units.literal: On the railing seat on all four sides were red-lacquered strip ring panels.

units.zh: 前左右有門，高四尺五寸有奇，廣二尺二寸有奇。
units.en: Doors to the front left and right stood a little over four feet five inches high and a little over two feet two inches wide.
units.literal: To the front left and right were doors a little over four feet five inches high and a little over two feet two inches wide.

units.zh: 門旁槅各二及明栨、後五山 屏風，皆紅髹，用抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。
units.en: Beside each door stood two panels and open lattices; the rear five-peak screen was red-lacquered and fitted with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.
units.literal: Beside each door were two panels and open lattices; at the rear a five-peak screen—all lacquered red, set with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.

units.zh: 亭底紅髹，施紅花毯、紅錦褥席。
units.en: The pavilion floor was red-lacquered, furnished with a red floral carpet and red brocade mats.
units.literal: The pavilion floor was lacquered red; a red floral carpet and red brocade mat and cushion were spread.

units.zh: 其椅 靠、坐褥、帷幔、紅簾之制，俱同金輅。
units.en: Its chair back, seat cushions, curtains, and red curtains all matched the gold carriage.
units.literal: Its chair back, seat cushions, curtains, and red curtain specifications were all the same as the gold carriage.

units.zh: 輅頂並圓盤，高二尺四寸有奇，用抹金 銅寶珠頂，餘同金輅。
units.en: The carriage top and round disk together rose a little over two feet four inches, with a gilt-bronze jeweled finial; the rest matched the gold carriage.
units.literal: The carriage top and round disk together were a little over two feet four inches high, using a gilt-bronze precious-pearl finial; the rest was the same as the gold carriage.

units.zh: 天輪三層，皆紅髹，上雕木貼金邊耀葉板六十三片，內飾 青地雕木五彩雲文三層，間繪五彩雲襯板六十三片，四周黃銅裝釘。
units.en: The three red-lacquered heaven-wheel layers bore sixty-three carved gilt-edged radiant leaf plates above, three layers of carved five-colored clouds on blue within, sixty-three painted cloud backing plates between, and yellow-bronze nail fittings on all four sides.
units.literal: The heaven-wheel had three layers, all lacquered red; above were sixty-three carved wooden gilt-edged radiant leaf plates; within were three layers of carved wooden five-colored cloud patterns on blue ground, alternating with sixty-three painted five-colored cloud backing plates; on all four sides were yellow-bronze nail fittings.

units.zh: 上施紅綺瀝 水三層，每層八十一摺，繡瑞草文。
units.en: Three layers of red damask drip panels hung above, each with eighty-one folds and embroidered with auspicious herb motifs.
units.literal: Above were set three layers of red damask drip-water hangings, each layer of eighty-one folds, embroidered with auspicious herb patterns.

units.zh: 前垂青綺絡帶二，俱繡升龍五彩雲文。
units.en: Two green damask net bands hung at the front, both embroidered with ascending dragons among five-colored clouds.
units.literal: In front hung two green damask net bands, both embroidered with ascending-dragon five-colored cloud patterns.

units.zh: 圓盤 四角連輅座板，用攀頂紅線圓條四，並紅髹木魚。
units.en: The four corners of the round disk joined the carriage seat boards, with four red cord roundels from the finial and red-lacquered wooden fish fittings.
units.literal: The four corners of the round disk connected to the carriage seat boards, using four red cord round strips from the climbing top, together with red-lacquered wooden fish.

units.zh: 亭前後闌干同金輅，左右闌干 各一扇，內嵌條環板，皆紅髹。
units.en: The pavilion's front and rear balustrades matched the gold carriage; one balustrade panel stood to each side, all red-lacquered with inset strip ring panels.
units.literal: The pavilion's front and rear balustrades were the same as the gold carriage; left and right balustrades one panel each; within were inset strip ring panels, all lacquered red.

units.zh: 計十四柱，柱首雕木紅蓮花，線金青綠裝蓮花抱 柱，前闌干內布花毯。
units.en: There were fourteen pillars capped with carved red lotuses, with gold-thread blue-green lotus embrace-pillars; a floral carpet was spread within the front balustrade.
units.literal: In all fourteen pillars; the pillar heads were carved wooden red lotuses; gold-thread blue-green enamel lotus embrace-pillars; within the front balustrade a floral carpet was spread.

units.zh: 紅旗二，與金輅所樹同，竿上只垂紅纓五。
units.en: Two red flags matched those raised on the gold carriage, with only five red tassels hanging from each pole.
units.literal: Two red flags, the same as those erected on the gold carriage; on the pole only five red tassels hung down.

units.zh: 其踏梯、行馬 之屬，亦同金輅。
units.en: Its mounting ladder, traveling-horse frames, and the like also matched the gold carriage.
units.literal: Its mounting ladder, traveling-horse frames, and the like were also the same as the gold carriage.

units.zh: 帳房用綠色螭頭，餘與東宮同。
units.en: The tent chamber bore green chih-dragon finials; otherwise it matched the Eastern Palace specifications.
units.literal: The tent chamber used green chih-dragon heads; the rest was the same as the Eastern Palace.

units.zh: 親王妃車，亦曰鳳轎、小轎，制俱同東宮妃。
units.en: The imperial prince's consort's carriage, also called the phoenix or small palanquin, followed the Eastern Palace consort's specifications entirely.
units.literal: The imperial prince's consort's carriage, also called the phoenix palanquin or small palanquin, specifications all the same as the Eastern Palace consort.

units.zh: 惟鳳轎衣用木紅平羅。
units.en: Only the phoenix palanquin cover was made of tree-red plain gauze.
units.literal: Only the phoenix palanquin cover used tree-red plain gauze.

units.zh: 小轎衣 二：一用礬紅素紵絲，一用木紅平羅。
units.en: There were two small palanquin covers: one of plain alum-red pongee silk and one of tree-red plain gauze.
units.literal: Small palanquin covers two: one used alum-red plain pongee silk, one used tree-red plain gauze.

units.zh: 行障、坐障，制同東宮妃。
units.en: Its traveling and seated screens matched the Eastern Palace consort's specifications.
units.literal: Traveling screens and seated screens: specifications the same as the Eastern Palace consort.

units.zh: 公主車，宋用厭翟車，明初因之。
units.en: Imperial princesses' carriages: the Song used the yan-di carriage, and early Ming followed suit.
units.literal: Princess carriages: under Song they used the yan-di carriage; early Ming followed this.

units.zh: 其後定制，鳳轎、行障、坐障，如親王妃。
units.en: Later regulations specified phoenix palanquins, traveling screens, and seated screens like those of an imperial prince's consort.
units.literal: Thereafter fixed regulations: phoenix palanquin, traveling screens, seated screens, like the imperial prince's consort.

units.zh: 皇孫車，永樂中，定皇太孫婚禮儀仗如親王，降皇太子一等，而用象輅。
units.en: During Yongle, the imperial heir's son was granted wedding ceremonial guard like a prince, one rank below the crown prince, with an ivory carriage.
units.literal: Imperial grandson carriages: in the Yongle reign, it was fixed that the heir apparent's son's wedding ceremonial guard was like an imperial prince, one rank below the crown prince, using the ivory carriage.

units.zh: 郡王無輅，只有帳房，制同親王。
units.en: Commandery princes were granted no state carriage, only tent chambers matching those of imperial princes.
units.literal: Commandery princes had no carriage; they only had tent chambers, specifications the same as imperial princes.

units.zh: 郡王妃及郡主俱用翟轎，制與皇妃鳳轎同，第易鳳爲翟。
units.en: Commandery princes' consorts and commandery ladies used di palanquins built like imperial consorts' phoenix palanquins, but with pheasants in place of phoenixes.
units.literal: Commandery prince's consorts and commandery ladies all used the di palanquin; specifications the same as the imperial consort's phoenix palanquin, but changing phoenix to di.

units.zh: 行障、坐障同親王 妃，而繪雲翟文。
units.en: Their traveling and seated screens matched an imperial prince's consort's, but were painted with cloud and pheasant motifs.
units.literal: Traveling screens and seated screens the same as the imperial prince's consort, but painted with cloud-di patterns.

units.zh: 百官乘車之制：洪武元年令，凡車不得雕飾龍鳳文。
units.en: Regulations for officials' carriages: a Hongwu first-year order forbade dragon or phoenix ornament on any carriage.
units.literal: Regulations for all officials' carriages: the first year of Hongwu order, all carriages were not permitted carved dragon-phoenix ornament.

units.zh: 職官一品至三品，用間 金飾銀螭繡帶，青縵。
units.en: Ranks one through three used awnings with gold-spaced silver chih-dragon embroidered bands and blue covers.
units.literal: Officials of ranks one through three used spaced gold-decorated silver chih-dragon embroidered bands and blue awnings.

units.zh: 四品五品，素獅頭繡帶，青縵。
units.en: Ranks four and five used plain lion-head embroidered bands and blue awnings.
units.literal: Ranks four and five, plain lion-head embroidered bands, blue awnings.

units.zh: 六品至九品，用素雲頭青 帶，青縵。
units.en: Ranks six through nine used plain cloud-head blue bands and blue awnings.
units.literal: Ranks six through nine used plain cloud-head blue bands, blue awnings.

units.zh: 轎同車制。
units.en: Palanquins followed the same regulations as carriages.
units.literal: Palanquins followed the carriage regulations.

units.zh: 庶民車及轎，並用黑油，齊頭平頂，皁縵，禁用雲頭。
units.en: Commoners' carriages and palanquins were black-lacquered with flat tops and black awnings; cloud-head ornament was forbidden.
units.literal: Commoners' carriages and palanquins all used black oil, flush-head flat-top, black awnings; cloud-heads were forbidden.

units.zh: 六 年令，凡車轎禁丹漆，五品以上車止用青縵。
units.en: A sixth-year order banned cinnabar lacquer on all carriages and palanquins; carriages of the fifth rank and above were limited to blue awnings.
units.literal: Sixth-year order: all carriages and palanquins forbade cinnabar lacquer; carriages of rank five and above used only blue awnings.

units.zh: 婦女許坐轎，官民老疾者亦得乘之。
units.en: Women were allowed palanquins, and aged or infirm officials and commoners could ride them as well.
units.literal: Women were permitted to ride palanquins; officials and commoners who were old or infirm also obtained permission to ride them.

units.zh: 景泰四年令，在京三品以上得乘轎。
units.en: A Jingtai fourth-year order allowed officials of the third rank and above in the capital to ride palanquins.
units.literal: Fourth year of Jingtai order: in the capital, rank three and above obtained permission to ride palanquins.

units.zh: 弘治七年令，文武官例應乘轎者，以四人舁 之。
units.en: A Hongzhi seventh-year order required civil and military officials entitled to palanquins to be carried by four bearers.
units.literal: Seventh year of Hongzhi order: civil and military officials for whom palanquin riding was standard were borne by four men.

units.zh: 其五府管事，內外鎮守、守備及公、侯、伯、都督等，不問老少，皆不得乘 轎，違例乘轎及擅用八人者，奏聞。
units.en: Stewards of the Five Chief Offices, garrison and defense commanders, dukes, marquises, earls, and regional commanders were barred from palanquins regardless of age; violations and unauthorized use of eight bearers were reported to the throne.
units.literal: The Five Chief Offices stewards, inner and outer garrison commanders, defense commanders, dukes, marquises, earls, regional commanders, and the like, regardless of age, all were not permitted to ride palanquins; those who violated regulations by riding palanquins or presumptuously using eight bearers were reported to the throne.

units.zh: 蓋自太祖不欲勳臣廢騎射，雖上公，出必乘 馬。
units.en: The founding emperor had wished to keep meritorious officials skilled in mounted archery; even the highest nobles were expected to ride when abroad.
units.literal: This was because from the founding emperor's time he did not wish meritorious ministers to abandon mounted archery; even highest nobles, going out inevitably rode horses.

units.zh: 永樂元年，駙馬都尉胡觀越制乘晉王濟熹朱<車尞>棕轎，爲給事中周景所劾。
units.en: In Yongle's first year, Imperial Son-in-law Commandant Hu Guan exceeded his rank by riding Prince Ji Xi of Jin's red-framed brown palanquin and was impeached by Supervising Secretary Zhou Jing.
units.literal: First year of Yongle, imperial son-in-law Commandant Hu Guan exceeded regulations by riding Prince Ji Xi of Jin's red-framed brown palanquin, and was impeached by Supervising Secretary Zhou Jing.

units.zh: 有詔宥觀而賜濟熹書，切責之。
units.en: An edict pardoned Guan but sent Ji Xi a letter of sharp rebuke.
units.literal: There was an edict pardoning Guan and bestowing Ji Xi a letter, sternly reprimanding him.

units.zh: 惟文職大臣乘轎，庶官亦乘馬。
units.en: Only senior civil officials rode palanquins; lesser officials rode horses as well.
units.literal: Only civil chief ministers rode palanquins; common officials also rode horses.

units.zh: 又文臣皆許乘 車，大臣得乘安車。
units.en: Civil officials were also permitted carriages, and senior ministers might ride the secure carriage.
units.literal: Moreover all civil ministers were permitted to ride carriages; chief ministers obtained permission to ride the secure carriage.

units.zh: 後久廢不用。
units.en: This practice was later abandoned for a long time.
units.literal: Later this was long abandoned and unused.

units.zh: 正德四年，禮部侍郎劉機言，《大明集禮》， 公卿大臣得乘安車，因請定轎扇傘蓋品級等差。
units.en: In Zhengde's fourth year, Vice Minister of Rites Liu Ji cited the Collected Rites of Great Ming, which granted secure carriages to dukes and ministers, and asked that rank gradations for palanquins, fans, parasols, and canopies be fixed.
units.literal: Fourth year of Zhengde, Vice Minister of Rites Liu Ji spoke: the Collected Rites of Great Ming states that dukes and ministers obtain permission to ride the secure carriage; he therefore requested fixing palanquin, fan, parasol, and canopy rank gradations.

units.zh: 帝以京城內安車傘蓋久不行，卻 其請，而命轎扇俱如例行。
units.en: The emperor rejected the request because secure carriages, parasols, and canopies had long fallen out of use in the capital, and ordered palanquins and fans to follow ordinary practice.
units.literal: The emperor, on the grounds that within the capital secure carriages, parasols, and canopies had long gone unpracticed, rejected his request, and ordered palanquins and fans all to follow routine practice.

units.zh: 嘉靖十五年，禮部尚書霍韜言：「禮儀定式，京官三 品以上乘轎，邇者文官皆用肩輿，或乘女轎。
units.en: In Jiajing's fifteenth year, Minister of Rites Huo Tao said: "The Prescribed Rites allow capital officials of the third rank and above palanquins, yet lately civil officials all use shoulder litters or women's palanquins.
units.literal: Fifteenth year of Jiajing, Minister of Rites Huo Tao spoke: "In the Prescribed Rites, capital officials of rank three and above ride palanquins; recently civil officials all use shoulder litters, or ride women's palanquins.

units.zh: 乞申明禮制，俾臣下有所遵守。」
units.en: I ask that the ritual regulations be clearly restated so officials may know what to follow."
units.literal: I beg to clarify the ritual regulations, so that ministers below may have something to observe."

units.zh: 乃定四品下不許乘轎，亦毋得用肩輿。
units.en: The court then barred officials below the fourth rank from palanquins and from shoulder litters as well.
units.literal: Thereupon it was fixed that below rank four palanquins were not permitted, and shoulder litters also were not to be used.

units.zh: 隆慶二年，給事中徐尚劾應城伯孫文棟等 乘轎出入，驕僣無狀。
units.en: In Longqing's second year, Supervising Secretary Xu Shang impeached Yingcheng Earl Sun Wendong and others for riding palanquins in public with outrageous presumption.
units.literal: Second year of Longqing, Supervising Secretary Xu Shang impeached Yingcheng Earl Sun Wendong and others for riding palanquins in and out, arrogant and presumptuous beyond measure.

units.zh: 帝命奪文棟等俸。
units.en: The emperor ordered Wendong and the others stripped of salary.
units.literal: The emperor ordered Wendong's and the others' salaries seized.

units.zh: 乃諭兩京武職非奉特恩不許乘轎，文官 四品以下用帷轎者，禁如例。
units.en: Edicts to both capitals then barred military officers from palanquins unless specially favored, and forbade civil officials below the fourth rank curtained palanquins as before.
units.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued to both capitals that military offices, unless granted special favor, were not permitted to ride palanquins; civil officials below rank four using curtained palanquins were forbidden as per precedent.

units.zh: 萬曆三年奏定勳戚及武臣不許用帷轎、肩輿並交牀 上馬。
units.en: In Wanli's third year it was decreed that meritorious kin and military officers might not use curtained palanquins, shoulder litters, or mounting stools to mount their horses.
units.literal: Third year of Wanli memorial fixed that meritorious kin and military ministers were not permitted to use curtained palanquins, shoulder litters, and mounting-stool horse mounting.

units.zh: 至若破格殊典，則宣德中少保黃淮陪遊西苑，嘗乘肩輿入禁中。
units.en: Extraordinary exceptions did occur: during Xuande, Junior Guardian Huang Huai once rode a shoulder litter into the forbidden precinct while touring the Western Park.
units.literal: As for violations of rank and special precedents: in Xuande's reign Junior Guardian Huang Huai accompanied tours of the Western Park and once rode a shoulder litter into the forbidden precinct.

units.zh: 嘉靖間， 嚴嵩奉詔苑直，年及八旬，出入得乘肩輿。
units.en: During Jiajing, Yan Song, ordered to serve at the imperial park at age eighty, was permitted a shoulder litter when coming and going.
units.literal: During Jiajing, Yan Song received an edict to serve at the park, his years reaching eighty; going in and out he obtained permission to ride a shoulder litter.

units.zh: 武臣則郭勳、朱希忠特命乘肩輿扈南 巡蹕，後遂賜常乘焉。
units.en: Military officers Guo Xun and Zhu Xizhong were specially permitted shoulder litters on the southern tour, and later granted them for regular use.
units.literal: Among military ministers Guo Xun and Zhu Xizhong were specially ordered to ride shoulder litters escorting the southern tour retinue; afterward they were granted regular use.

units.zh: 皆非制也。
units.en: None of these conformed to regulation.
units.literal: All were not according to regulation.

units.zh: 傘蓋之制：洪武元年，令庶民不得用羅絹涼傘，但許用油紙雨傘。
units.en: Parasol and canopy regulations: a Hongwu first-year order barred commoners from silk cool parasols and allowed only oiled-paper rain umbrellas.
units.literal: Regulations for parasols and canopies: first year of Hongwu, ordered that commoners were not permitted to use gauze-silk cool parasols; only oiled-paper rain umbrellas were allowed.

units.zh: 三年，令 京城內一品二品用傘蓋，其餘用雨傘。
units.en: A third-year order allowed only ranks one and two parasol-canopies within the capital; all others used rain umbrellas.
units.literal: Third year, ordered that within the capital ranks one and two used parasol-canopies; the rest used rain umbrellas.

units.zh: 十六年，令尚書、侍郎、左右都御史、通 政使、太常卿、應天府尹、國子祭酒、翰林學士許張傘蓋。
units.en: A sixteenth-year order permitted ministers, vice ministers, censors-in-chief, transmission commissioners, grand court ceremonialists, the Yingtian prefect, the imperial academy chancellor, and Hanlin academicians to use parasols and canopies.
units.literal: Sixteenth year, ordered that ministers, vice ministers, left and right censors-in-chief, transmission commissioners, grand court ceremonialists, Yingtian prefect, imperial academy chancellor, and Hanlin academicians were permitted to deploy parasols and canopies.

units.zh: 二十六年定一品、二 品傘用銀浮屠頂，三品、四品用紅浮屠頂，俱用黑色茶褐羅表，紅絹裹，三檐；
units.en: In the twenty-sixth year ranks one and two were assigned silver pagoda-finial parasols and ranks three and four red pagoda-finial parasols, all with black tea-brown gauze exteriors, red silk linings, and three tiers;
units.literal: Twenty-sixth year fixed: ranks one and two parasols used silver pagoda finials; ranks three and four used red pagoda finials; all used black tea-brown gauze exterior, red silk lining, three tiers;

units.zh: 雨傘用紅油絹。
units.en: Their rain umbrellas were of red oiled silk.
units.literal: Rain umbrellas used red oiled silk.

units.zh: 五品紅浮屠頂，青羅表，紅絹裹，兩檐；
units.en: Rank five used red pagoda-finial parasols with blue gauze exteriors, red silk linings, and two tiers;
units.literal: Rank five: red pagoda finial, blue gauze exterior, red silk lining, two tiers;

units.zh: 雨傘同。
units.en: Rain umbrellas followed the same rule.
units.literal: Rain umbrellas the same.

units.zh: 四品、六品至 九品，用紅浮屠頂，青絹表，紅絹裹，兩檐；
units.en: Ranks four and six through nine used red pagoda-finial parasols with blue silk exteriors, red silk linings, and two tiers;
units.literal: Ranks four and six through nine used red pagoda finials, blue silk exterior, red silk lining, two tiers;

units.zh: 雨傘俱用油紙。
units.en: Their rain umbrellas were all oiled paper.
units.literal: Rain umbrellas all used oiled paper.

units.zh: 三十五年，官員傘 蓋不許用金繡，朱丹裝飾。
units.en: In the thirty-fifth year officials were forbidden gold embroidery or cinnabar ornament on parasols and canopies.
units.literal: Thirty-fifth year, officials' parasols and canopies were not permitted gold embroidery or cinnabar-red decoration.

units.zh: 公、侯、駙馬、伯與一品、二品同。
units.en: Dukes, marquises, imperial sons-in-law, and earls followed the rank-one and rank-two specifications.
units.literal: Dukes, marquises, imperial sons-in-law, and earls were the same as ranks one and two.

units.zh: 成化九年，令兩 京官遇雨任用油傘，其涼傘不許張於京城。
units.en: A Chenghua ninth-year order allowed officials in both capitals to use oiled umbrellas in rain, but forbade opening cool parasols within the capital.
units.literal: Ninth year of Chenghua, ordered that officials of both capitals when encountering rain could use oiled umbrellas at discretion; cool parasols were not permitted opened within the capital.

units.zh: 鞍轡之制：洪武六年，令庶民不得描金，惟銅鐵裝飾。
units.en: Saddle and bridle regulations: a Hongwu sixth-year order barred commoners from gold tracery and allowed only copper and iron ornament.
units.literal: Regulations for saddles and bridles: sixth year of Hongwu, ordered that commoners were not permitted gold tracery, only copper and iron ornament.

units.zh: 二十六年，定公、侯、 一品、二品用銀，鐵事件，<革佔>用描銀。
units.en: In the twenty-sixth year dukes, marquises, and ranks one and two were assigned silver fittings and leather flaps with silver tracery.
units.literal: Twenty-sixth year fixed: dukes, marquises, ranks one and two used silver, iron fittings; saddle flaps used silver tracery.

units.zh: 三品至五品，用銀，鐵事件， <革佔>用油畫。
units.en: Ranks three through five used silver fittings and oil-painted leather flaps.
units.literal: Ranks three through five used silver, iron fittings; saddle flaps used oil painting.

units.zh: 六品至九品，用擺錫，鐵事件，<革佔>用油畫。
units.en: Ranks six through nine used pewter plating, iron fittings, and oil-painted leather flaps.
units.literal: Ranks six through nine used pewter plating, iron fittings; saddle flaps used oil painting.

units.zh: 三十五年，官民人等 馬頷下纓並鞦轡俱用黑色，不許紅纓及描金、嵌金、天青、硃紅裝飾。
units.en: In the thirty-fifth year chin tassels and crupper bridles for all were restricted to black, barring red tassels and gold tracery, inlaid gold, sky-blue, or cinnabar ornament.
units.literal: Thirty-fifth year, officials and commoners alike: horses' chin tassels and crupper bridles all used black; red tassels and gold tracery, inlaid gold, sky-blue, and cinnabar-red ornament were not permitted.

units.zh: 軍民用 鐵事件，黑綠油<革佔>。
units.en: Soldiers and commoners used iron fittings and black-green oiled leather flaps.
units.literal: Military and commoners used iron fittings, black-green oiled saddle flaps.

units.zh: 尚書敬顯儁曰：「孔子云：『微管仲，吾其被發左衽矣』以此言之，右衽為是。」
units.en: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."
units.literal: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."

units.zh: 洪武四年七月，蜀夏明升降表至京師，太祖命中書集議受降禮。
units.en: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Hongwu, Ming Sheng of Shu-Xia presented a surrender memorial at the capital; the founding emperor ordered the Secretariat to convene deliberation on the rite of receiving surrender.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Hongwu, Ming Sheng of Shu-Xia presented a surrender memorial at the capital; the founding emperor ordered the Secretariat to convene deliberation on the rite of receiving surrender.

units.zh: 帝以昶專治國政，所爲奢縱，升年幼，事由臣下，免其叩頭伏地上表請罪禮，惟命升及其官屬朝見，百官朝賀。
units.en: The emperor held that Meng Chang had personally governed state affairs and acted with extravagance and license, while Ming Sheng was young and affairs were decided by his ministers; he exempted them from the rite of knocking the head and prostrating to present a memorial pleading guilt, ordering only that Ming Sheng and his officials attend audience while the officials offered congratulation.
units.literal: The emperor held that Chang had personally governed state affairs and acted with extravagance and license, while Ming Sheng was young and matters were decided by his ministers; he exempted them from the rite of knocking the head and prostrating on the ground to present a memorial pleading guilt, ordering only that Ming Sheng and his officials attend audience while the officials offered congratulation.

units.zh: 帝不許，事詳《本紀》。
units.en: The emperor did not consent; details are given in the Basic Annals.
units.literal: The emperor did not consent; details are in the Basic Annals.

units.zh: 帝御奉天殿，皇太子親王侍，百官朝服陪列，達、文忠奉表賀。
units.en: The emperor presided in the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the crown prince and imperial princes attended; officials in court dress stood in attendance as Xu Da and Wenzhong presented the memorial of congratulation.
units.literal: The emperor presided in the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the crown prince and imperial princes attended; officials in court dress stood in attendance; Xu Da and Wenzhong presented the memorial in congratulation.

units.zh: 洪武三年六月，左副將軍李文忠北征大捷，遣官送所俘元孫買的裏八剌及寶冊至京師。
units.en: In the sixth month of the third year of Hongwu, Left Deputy General Li Wenzhong won a great victory on the northern campaign and dispatched officials to bring to the capital the Yuan imperial grandson Maidibali and the precious registers among the captives.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Hongwu, the Left Deputy General Li Wenzhong won a great victory on the northern campaign and dispatched officials to send to the capital the Yuan imperial grandson Maidibali and the precious registers among the captives.

units.zh: 洪武元年閏七月，詔定軍禮。
units.en: In the intercalary seventh month of the first year of Hongwu, an edict established military ceremonial regulations.
units.literal: In the intercalary seventh month of the first year of Hongwu, an edict fixed military rites.

units.zh: 復謂省臣曰：「故國之妃朝於君者，元有此禮，不必效之。」
units.en: He further told the provincial officials: "When a consort of a fallen state has audience with the sovereign, the Yuan had such a rite, but there is no need to imitate it."
units.literal: He further told the provincial officials: "When a consort of a fallen state has audience with the sovereign, the Yuan had such a rite, but there is no need to imitate it."

units.zh: 百官請行獻俘禮。
units.en: The officials requested performance of the captive-presentation rite.
units.literal: The officials requested that the captive-presentation rite be performed.

units.zh: 隆慶二年，大學士張居正言：「祖宗時有大閱禮，乞親臨校閱。」
units.en: In the second year of Longqing, Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng said: "In the time of our ancestors there was a grand review rite; I beg Your Majesty to come in person to inspect and review."
units.literal: In the second year of Longqing, Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng said: "In the time of our ancestors there was a grand review rite; I beg Your Majesty to come in person to inspect and review."

units.zh: 前期一日，皇帝常服告於內殿，行四拜禮，如出郊儀。
units.en: One day in advance, the emperor in ordinary dress announced at the inner hall and performed four bows, as in the suburban departure protocol.
units.literal: One day in advance, the emperor in ordinary dress announced at the inner hall and performed four bows, as in the suburban departure protocol.

units.zh: 皇帝常服乘輦由長安左門出，官軍導從，鉦鼓振作。
units.en: The emperor in ordinary dress rode the palanquin out through the left Chang'an Gate; officers and soldiers led the escort as gongs and drums struck up.
units.literal: The emperor in ordinary dress rode the palanquin out through the left Chang'an Gate; officers and soldiers led the escort; gongs and drums struck up.

units.zh: 皇帝升輦。
units.en: The emperor ascended the palanquin.
units.literal: The emperor ascended the palanquin.

units.zh: 越二日，皇帝御皇極門，賜敕勉勵將士。
units.en: Two days later the emperor presided at the Huangji Gate and bestowed an edict encouraging the officers and soldiers.
units.literal: Two days later the emperor presided at the Huangji Gate and bestowed an edict encouraging the officers and soldiers.

units.zh: 命於明年八月舉行。
units.en: An order was issued to hold it in the eighth month of the following year.
units.literal: An order was issued to hold it in the eighth month of the following year.

units.zh: 璁更為《大禮或問》以進，而主事霍韜、桂萼，給事中熊浹議與璁合。
units.en: Zhang Cong also wrote "Questions on the Great Rites"; Huo Tao and Gui E, section directors, and Xiong Jia, supervising secretary, agreed with him.
units.literal: Cong further composed "Questions on the Great Rites" and presented it; Section Director Huo Tao and Gui E, and Supervising Secretary Xiong Shi, argued in agreement with Cong.

units.zh: 進士張璁上書請考興獻王，帝大悅。
units.en: Presented scholar Zhang Cong memorialized to worship Prince Xingxian; Jiajing was delighted.
units.literal: The presented scholar Zhang Cong submitted a memorial requesting sacrifice to Prince Xingxian; the emperor was greatly pleased.

units.zh: 十一月，青州黃巾寇太山，太山太守應劭擊破之。
units.en: In the eleventh month Qingzhou Yellow Turbans invaded Taishan; Ying Shao, the governor, drove them off.
units.literal: In the eleventh month, the Qingzhou Yellow Turbans raided Mount Tai, and Mount Tai Governor Ying Shao attacked and defeated them.

units.zh: 秋七月，司空种拂免，光祿大夫濟南淳于嘉為司空。
units.en: In the seventh month Chong Fu left the ministry of works; Chunyu Jia of Jinan, grandee of brilliant candidacy, replaced him.
units.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Minister of Works Chong Fu was dismissed, and Grandee of Brilliant Candidacy Chunyu Jia of Jinan was made Minister of Works.

units.zh: 穆宗，契天隆道淵懿寬仁顯文光武純德弘孝莊皇帝，諱載垕，世宗第三子也。
units.en: Emperor Muzong—honored after death as one who manifested Heaven, upheld the grand Way, and united profound graciousness, broad benevolence, brilliant culture, glorious martial accomplishment, pure virtue, expansive filial piety, and solemnity—was named Zhu Zaihou and was the third son of Emperor Shizong.
units.literal: Muzong, the Emperor of Manifesting Heaven, Upholding the Grand Way, Profound and Gracious, Broad and Benevolent, Brilliant in Culture, Glorious in Martial Accomplishment, Pure in Virtue, Expansive in Filial Piety and Solemnity, taboo name Zaihou, was Shizong's third son.

units.zh: 已而莊敬薨，世宗以王長且賢，繼序已定，而中外危疑，屢有言者，乃令景王之國。
units.en: When Crown Prince Zhuangjing died soon after, Shizong—holding that the Prince of Yu was eldest and worthy and the succession already settled, though court and realm remained uneasy and many spoke out—sent Prince Jing to his fief.
units.literal: Thereafter Crown Prince Zhuangjing died; Shizong, because the prince was eldest and worthy and the succession was already settled, yet court and realm were uneasy and many spoke out, ordered Prince Jing to depart for his fief.

units.zh: 四十五年十二月庚子，世宗崩。
units.en: In the twelfth month of Jiajing forty-five, on gengzi, Shizong died.
units.literal: Jiajing year forty-five, twelfth month, day gengzi: Shizong died.

units.zh: 十二月庚寅，世宗神主祔太廟。
units.en: In the twelfth month, on gengyin, Shizong's spirit tablet was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
units.literal: Twelfth month, day gengyin: Shizong's spirit tablet was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

units.zh: 三月壬申，葬肅皇帝於永陵。
units.en: In the third month, on renshen, the late Shizong was buried at Yongling.
units.literal: Third month, day renshen: the Su Emperor was buried at Yongling.

units.zh: 嘉靖十八年二月封裕王，與莊敬太子、景恭王同日受冊。
units.en: In the second month of Jiajing eighteen he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yu, invested on the same day as Crown Prince Zhuangjing and Prince Jing Gong.
units.literal: In Jiajing year eighteen, second month, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yu, receiving investiture on the same day as Crown Prince Zhuangjing and Prince Jing Gong.

units.zh: 八月壬子，侍讀解缙、編修黄淮入直文淵閣。
units.en: In the eighth month, on renzi, Reader-in-Waiting Xie Jin and Compiler Huang Huai took up duty in the Wenyuan Pavilion.
units.literal: In the eighth month, on the renzi day, Reader-in-Waiting Xie Jin and Compiler Huang Huai entered attendance at the Wenyuan Pavilion.

units.zh: 帝以元制不足法，令詹同考歷代東宮官制，選勳德老成及新進賢者，兼領東宮官。
units.en: Hongwu rejected the Yuan precedent, had Zhan Tong study Eastern Palace institutions of past dynasties, and appointed both veteran meritorious officials and promising newcomers to dual posts in the heir apparent's establishment.
units.literal: The emperor held that the Yuan system was not worth taking as model, ordered Zhan Tong to examine the Eastern Palace offices of successive dynasties, and selected men of merit and long experience together with newly advanced worthies to hold Eastern Palace posts concurrently.

units.zh: 洪武元年正月，立為皇太子。
units.en: In the first month of Hongwu's first year he was made crown prince.
units.literal: In the first month of the first year of Hongwu, he was installed as crown prince.

units.zh: 十六年，以武定侯郭勳奏，進其祖英。
units.en: In the sixteenth year, at Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun’s memorial, his grandfather Ying was advanced.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year, at Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun’s memorial, his grandfather Ying was advanced.

units.zh: 而禮部尚書嚴嵩等言：「靈駕北來，慈宮南詣，共一舉耳。
units.en: Minister of Rites Yan Song argued: "The imperial coffin travels north while the Kind Palace goes south—one journey serves both.
units.literal: But Minister of Rites Yan Song and others said: "The imperial coffin comes north and the Kind Palace goes south—it is a single undertaking.

units.zh: 大峪可朝發夕至，顯陵遠在承天，恐陛下春秋念之。
units.en: Dayu lies a day's march away, but Xianling is distant at Chengtian; we fear Your Majesty's advancing years will be burdened by the distance.
units.literal: Dayu can be reached setting out in the morning and arriving by evening; Xianling is far away at Chengtian—we fear Your Majesty, in the autumn of life, will brood on it.

units.zh: 臣謂如初議便。」
units.en: Your servant thinks the first plan is better."
units.literal: Your subject holds that the original proposal is convenient."

units.zh: 十七年十二月崩，諭禮、工二部將改葬獻皇帝于大峪山，以駙馬都尉京山侯崔元為奉迎行禮使，兵部尚書張瓚為禮儀護行使，指揮趙俊為吉凶儀仗官，翊國公郭勳知聖母山陵事。
units.en: In the twelfth month of the seventeenth year she died. Jiajing ordered the Ministries of Rites and Works to move the Xian emperor to Dayu Mountain, naming Cui Yuan, commandant and Jingshan marquis, welcoming envoy; Zhang Zan, minister of war, ritual escort; Zhao Jun, commander, regalia officer; and Guo Xun, defender of the state, to manage the dowager's tomb.
units.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventeenth year she died; he instructed the Ministries of Rites and Works to reinter the Xian Emperor at Dayu Mountain, appointing Commandant-in-Chief of the Capital Guards and Jingshan Marquis Cui Yuan as envoy for welcoming and performing rites, Minister of War Zhang Zan as envoy for protecting ritual, Commander Zhao Jun as officer of auspicious and inauspicious regalia, and Defender of the State Duke Guo Xun to oversee the Holy Mother's tomb affairs.

units.zh: 四月，帝謁長陵，諭嚴嵩曰：「大峪不如純德。」
units.en: In the fourth month, visiting Changling, he told Yan Song: "Dayu is inferior to Chunde."
units.literal: In the fourth month the emperor worshipped at Changling and instructed Yan Song, saying: "Dayu is not as good as Chunde."

units.zh: 太祖所任張昶、楊憲、汪廣洋、胡惟庸皆獲罪，善長事寄如故。
units.en: Zhang Chang, Yang Xian, Wang Guangyang, and Hu Weiyong, whom the throne had raised, all fell for crime, yet Shanzhang's trust held.
units.literal: Zhang Chang, Yang Xian, Wang Guangyang, and Hu Weiyong, whom the Founding Emperor appointed, all fell into crime, yet Shanzhang's commission remained as before.

units.zh: 禮官跪於左，奏太宗體天弘道高明廣運聖武神功純仁至孝文皇帝謁辭。
units.en: A rites official knelt on the left and announced: "Taizong, Emperor who embodies Heaven, expands the Way, is lofty and bright, broadly carries fortune, sage in war and divine in accomplishment, purely benevolent and supremely filial, Cultured Emperor, pays his farewell visit."
units.literal: A rites official knelt on the left and announced: "Taizong, the Emperor who embodies Heaven, expands the Way, is lofty and bright, broadly carries fortune, sage in martial affairs and divine in accomplishment, purely benevolent and supremely filial, Cultured Emperor, pays his farewell visit."

units.zh: 內侍奏請太宗文皇帝神靈上神主。
units.en: Palace attendants announced a request that the spirit of Taizong, the Cultured Emperor, ascend to the spirit tablet.
units.literal: Palace attendants announced a request that the spirit of Taizong, Cultured Emperor, ascend to the spirit tablet.

units.zh: 典儀唱「太宗文皇帝謁廟」。
units.en: The master of ceremonies called out: "Taizong, the Cultured Emperor, pays visit to the temple."
units.literal: The master of ceremonies called out: "Taizong, Cultured Emperor, pays visit to the temple."

units.zh: 退朝，仍終太宗服制。
units.en: After retiring from court, he still observed the remainder of Taizong's mourning period.
units.literal: After retiring from court, he still completed Taizong's mourning period.

units.zh: 文帝崩於榆木川，遺詔一遵太祖遺制。
units.en: Emperor Wen died at Yumu River; his final testament followed Taizu's regulations in full.
units.literal: Emperor Wen passed away at Yumu River; his final testament wholly followed Taizu's final regulations.

units.zh: 十二月，禮部進葬祭儀：發引前三日，百官齋戒。
units.en: In the twelfth month, the Ministry of Rites presented the burial and sacrifice rites: three days before the funeral procession departed, all officials observed purification.
units.literal: In the twelfth month, the Ministry of Rites presented the burial and sacrifice rites: three days before the procession departed, all officials fasted and purified themselves.
